title: fix(data-objectstack): read the flat REST error envelope through one reader (objectui#9594)
body:
Fixes #9594

Clause-②: no

A console operator clicking "export to CSV" without the `allowExport` grant was shown one
word: `Forbidden`. The server had answered a sentence naming the object, the user and the
axis. This routes six hand-copied failure ladders in `ObjectStackAdapter` through one
internal envelope reader that understands every dialect on the wire.

Per the seat ruling on the card (option 2 carrying option 1's behaviour), the rung order is
`error.message` then `message` then a bare-string `error` then `statusText`.

## What changed

One new internal module, `packages/data-objectstack/src/error-envelope.ts`, exporting
`readErrorEnvelope(body)` which answers a message and a code. Six sites now call it:

| site | shape before | what it gets now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `searchAll` | full ladder to `statusText` | reader, plus the server `code` |
| `rawFindWithPopulate` | full ladder, already read `code` | reader; `code` precedence preserved exactly |
| `exportDownload` | full ladder to `statusText` | reader, plus the server `code` |
| `fetchObjectSchemaFresh` | full ladder to `statusText` | reader, plus the server `code` |
| `uploadFile` | `error.message` only, own fallback text | dialect reading only |
| `uploadFiles` | `error.message` only, own fallback text | dialect reading only |

The reader is deliberately **not** re-exported from the package entry point. Verified
mechanically: the export list of `src/index.ts` is byte-identical to base, 64 export lines
on both sides, so `Clause-②: no` holds.

## Mechanism assumptions, each re-measured on my own base

**1. The six sites are one ladder — PARTLY FALSIFIED, and the brief predicted where.**
The four `res.ok` ladders really are one shape, and the card's line numbers were all exact on
my base. The `statusText` pair is **not** the same shape: `uploadFile` / `uploadFiles` read
only `error.message`, fall back to a template rather than `statusText`, and throw
`ObjectStackError` with a hard-coded `UPLOAD_ERROR` code instead of a bare `Error` carrying
`status`. So they share the **dialect reading** and keep their own envelope — forcing their
last rung and their code through one function would have changed behaviour nobody asked for.
The card's phrase "the identical ladder is copied at five more sites" is accurate for four of
the six and loose for the upload pair.

**2. The flat dialect is still on the wire — CONFIRMED.** `@objectstack/rest` is not a
dependency of this repo, so I read the producer source in the sibling checkout, which
declares version `17.4.0` — the same version the card measured. `enforceExportPermission`
still writes `code` plus a string `error` plus `object`, with no `message` key.

**3. The affected-code count — RE-MEASURED INDEPENDENTLY, and it reproduces.** My scan walked
the producer's source tree rather than the shipped bundle the card used, brace-matching every
`.json(` body and keeping those with `code` and `error` and no `message`: 28 files, 68 matching
bodies, **34 distinct literal codes**. Diffed against the card's list: identical, zero
difference either way. `EXPORT_NOT_PERMITTED` was the known-hit control and it fired. A
different instrument reaching the same population is corroboration rather than a restatement.
Also measured: of those bodies, **zero** spell `error` equal to `code`, so the bare-string rung
always yields a real sentence for that family.

**4. The 401-vs-403 control — CONFIRMED, and it turned out to be load-bearing.** The 401 body
is `{ error: 'UNAUTHENTICATED', code: 'UNAUTHENTICATED', message: ... }`: flat, and its `error`
key holds the **code word** while the sentence lives in `message`. That is exactly why the
ruled rung order puts `message` before a string `error`. Inverting those two rungs would make
every unauthenticated response render the word `UNAUTHENTICATED` instead of its sentence. The
pair is pinned as a control at both the reader and the call site.

## Not a lenient fallback

Reading this dialect is conformance, not tolerance, and the producer's own text says so.
ADR-0112's 2026-07-30 amendment records the flat and wrapped envelopes as the two live,
sanctioned shapes, D5 leaves the flat one's fate an open maintainer question, and
`@objectstack/core`'s guidance beside `ANONYMOUS_DENY_BODY` states the rule: read the envelope
the seam you called DECLARES — flat from `/data` and `/meta`. Every site routed through the
reader calls a `/data` route. The server envelope is untouched; that belongs to objectstack#9559.

That same guidance names `body.error?.code ?? body.error` as precisely the chain an envelope
regression hides inside, so the reader takes `code` from `code` or a nested `error.code` and
**never** promotes a string `error` into that slot. A sentence is not a code.

## Decision on the card's optional extra (Zone 3)

The card floated appending `code` to the message text so an operator can search for
`EXPORT_NOT_PERMITTED`. **Taken, but as a structured field rather than in the text.** The four
`res.ok` ladders attach the server code to the thrown error. Reasons: `rawFindWithPopulate`
already did exactly this, so the other three now match it instead of drifting from it;
concatenating into `message` would corrupt the string every toolbar and i18n surface displays
and make the message unstable to assert on; and it gives the refusal tests a real `code` to
assert. The upload pair keeps `UPLOAD_ERROR` — putting a second, differently-sourced code on
one error with no declared precedence is the second de-facto contract AGENTS.md #0.1 bans.

## Tests, and proof they are not vacuous

`pnpm exec vitest run packages/data-objectstack/` — **67 files, 912 tests, all passing**, read
at `9cf9e0c6` (the merge commit, so after the last content change). Refusal cases assert `code`
and `status` together, never a bare throw.

Two ablations, in **opposite** directions, each mutated on disk through an anchor that had to
hit, with the injected and deleted text counted by `grep -c` on both sides and the restore
proven by `git diff HEAD` being empty and the blob hash matching HEAD:

- **Delete the bare-string rung** (reproduce the old blind spot): **6 tests red**, every one a
  flat-dialect case, across all three test files — and the 401 control stayed green.
- **Invert `message` and the string `error`**: **3 tests red**, every one a 401 case, and every
  403 case stayed green.

The two mutations turn **disjoint** sets red, which is what shows the 401 case is a genuine
control rather than a second copy of the 403 assertion. The call-site tests going red from a
mutation inside the reader module is also what proves the wiring is real at those sites.

No build was needed for either leg and none was run: the root vitest config aliases the
workspace packages to `src`, and the tests import the reader and the adapter by **relative**
path, so vitest compiles this tree's source directly. If source had not been what ran, no
mutation to it could have changed a verdict.

## Gates, exit code captured before any pipe

Derived from this repo's `package.json` scripts and `.github/workflows/`, against the real
diff. `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` was **not** used: it lives in the sibling repo and
derives families from the tree it runs in, so it cannot answer for this one.

| gate | exit |
| --- | --- |
| `check:new-line-citations` (Line Citation Gate) | 0 — "0 new citation(s)" |
| `check:control-bytes` | 0 |
| `check:changeset-presence` | 0 |
| `check:changeset-no-major` / `-overwrite` / `-fixed` / `-claims` | 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 |
| `check:pending-changeset-literals` | 0 |
| `check:unreferenced-sources` | 0 |
| `check:self-import` | 0 |
| `check:test-path-roots` | 0 |
| `check:vi-mock-specifiers` / `-inherit` / `-override-shape` | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| `check:readme-exports` | 0 after a full build |
| `check:dist-completeness --all` | 0 |
| `check:published-dist` | 0 |
| `check:published-tsconfig-exclude` | 0 |
| `check:esm-specifiers` | 0 |
| `check:entry-guard` | 0 |
| `check:side-effects-array` | 0 |
| `type-check` (this package) | 0 |
| `lint` (this package) | 0 |
| `check:node-esm-load` | 1 — environmental, see below |

`pnpm build` (whole workspace): 43 of 43 tasks successful.

**`check:readme-exports` first answered 1 and that reading was discarded, not reported.** Its
own output said the population had collapsed and named the cause — 34 unbuilt packages, all
four findings in `plugin-calendar` / `plugin-gantt` / `plugin-kanban` READMEs, none in this
package. After a full build it is 0 over a real population (58 keys compared, 0 unbuilt). A
prerequisite-not-met exit is not a failed measurement.

**`check:node-esm-load` answers 1 for a reason outside this branch.** Turbo shares one cache
across every worktree of a checkout, so the build replayed a **sibling agent worktree's**
artifacts (`objectui-issue-9568`) for five packages — `core`, `i18n`, `providers`,
`react-runtime`, `types` — and the gate refuses to grade what this tree did not produce rather
than greening over another tree's output. `@object-ui/data-objectstack` is **not** among the
refused: it was graded and its ESM entry loaded clean. The five are untouched by this diff, and
a clean CI checkout has no sibling worktree to inherit from. I force-rebuilt those five through
pnpm and the marker persisted, because the provenance marker is turbo's own task log and a
filtered pnpm build does not go through turbo; clearing it needs a full `TURBO_FORCE` rebuild
of the workspace, which I judged not worth several minutes of exclusive hold on this shared
container's verify lock to re-derive a fact about packages this branch does not touch.

The repo-wide `pnpm lint` and `pnpm test` are CI's runs. The lint narrowing here is declared and
measured: the root `eslint.config.js` is the only config (this package declares none), the
package's own `eslint .` — the exact per-package unit `turbo run lint` invokes — linted **76
files, 0 errors, 446 warnings** by its own `--format json` count, and type-aware linting is
**not** enabled (`tseslint.configs.recommended`, no `project` or `projectService`), so nothing
in this diff can move the verdict of a file it does not touch. Every warning is the
pre-existing `no-explicit-any` population; my appended export-test block adds none, and the
`searchAll` insert adds exactly one, in that file's established `fetchImpl as any` idiom.

## Acceptance notes

Observed and deliberately **not** filed:

- **A shared reader across packages.** objectui#7959 raised the same option for `app-shell`,
  and if both land, one reader shared across packages is the honest end state. Out of scope
  here by the card's own fence, and recorded rather than built. Successor: whichever of
  objectui#7959 / objectui#7938 / objectui#7368 lands next in this family.
- **Two more `statusText` sites that are not ladders and were left alone.** The discovery probe
  builds a `status` plus `statusText` string and never opens the body at all; the dataset-query
  throw already derives its detail through a separate classifier. Neither is an envelope read,
  so neither belongs to this reader. Successor: none — noted so the next reader of this module
  does not mistake the count of `statusText` mentions for the count of ladders.
- **Turbo's cross-worktree cache provenance**, above. Already known and handled by the gate,
  which names it and cites objectui#7276 — a condition of running several agents in one
  checkout, not a defect.
